guidance.Read_Me:
V1.0
FS Accumulator Structural Equivalency Spreadsheet Guide
The ASES template has been created to simplify the process of proving structural equivalency of the Tractive System Accumulator (TSAC).
Please enter your values in the yellow cells and paste all the images in the specific tabs which shows your entered values.
All dimensions and units must follow the European SI System!
The final decision about all designs will be made at technical inspection. Approval of an ASES does not guarantee passing Tech. Inspection nor a fully rules compliant accumulator!
As downloaded, the spreadsheet assumes a baseline steel/aluminium TSAC design. The majority of the cells in the spreadsheet are locked, you can only edit the cells shaded yellow. 
Cells shaded grey are dependant on the data entered in yellow cells, the formulae in these grey cells have been left visible so you can see how the results are calculated.
The vast majority of the tabs can be accessed using the hyperlinks on the cover sheet. If you enable macros when opening the document "Ctrl+e" will return you to the cover sheet.
The ASES has been extensively tested, but if you think you have found a mistake in the document or have any questions on how to use the template please submit a question in the usual manner.
Please read the guidance notes located at the end of the workbook.
If you find a new problem with the ASES template or require a clarification 72 hours or less before the ASES submission deadline please include your own proof of equivalency in the "Additional Info" tab and additionally submit a rules question.
Teams are not permitted to rename the name of the TAB or to delete any TAB.
Revisions:
V1.0
First release for 2026 rules
- TAB EV5.5.10-12 Cell Fixation: Updated name and sheet due to new rules.
- TAB EV5.5.14-18 Openings&Separation: Allowed N/A for some cases and removed
redundant check.
- TAB Datasheets Other Matl: Added cells for properties at 60 °C
- TAB Materials Overview: Fixed formula error
- TAB Materials Overview: Added cells for properties at 60 °C for Other Materials
- TAB Accumulator Pics: Removed name before "Material" for correction.

guidance.EV5.5.3 Guidance Notes:
ACCUMULATOR MATERIALS GUIDANCE NOTES
Materials except metallic and continuous fiber-reinforced laminates
Mechanical properties must be valid for ≥ 60 °C !
In general 3 possibilities to show compliance:
1. Values from Datasheet
- Must explicitly show mechanical properties at or above 60 °C.
- Glass transition/vicat temperature alone is not sufficient.
2. Values from own tests
- Test procedure shows mechanical properties ≥ 60 °C.
- Must be well documented (report, pictures).
3. Scientific justification
- Least favourable.
- Generous knock-down factor applied to ambient temperature values.
- Backed up by known behavior of the explicit material, must be explained scientifically.
BACK
guidance.EV5.5.9 Guidance Notes:
TSAC, STACK AND CELL FIXATION GUIDANCE NOTES
All mentioned parts and assembly mentioned in EV5.5.8, as well as the interface between
must withstand the mentioned accelerations.
This must be shown for every part/interface and every direction (x, y, z) in the respective
ASES tab.
For a quick review and pass, use the structure in the respective tab. This will help the 
reviewer to quickly understand your design and calculations.
Please note:
Analytical calculations always required, FEM can be supportive
Showing some flashy and colourfull FEM images without legends, full model description or 
unreadable numbers, no information on meshing etc. result in a "FAIL" directly.
Analytical calculations must at least be used to verify the FEM calculations.
BACK: Cell fixation

guidance.EV5.5.10-11 Guidance Notes:
CELL FIXATION GUIDANCE NOTES
Pouch cells must be fixed using one or both of the large 
surface(s) only.
Large surface means only the surface shown in the picture on the right.
This may be done by friction or adhesive.
The other surfaces of the cell must not carry any major load. However,
touching other surfaces for packaging reasons is acceptable.
Each used surface must be fixed on at least 80 %.
80 % is the absolute minimum surface to be used. If possible, use more
to distribute the force more evenly and improve safety.
Tabs of pouch cells must not carry mechanical loads and must not 
press into the pouch.
Absolutely no mechanical load is permitted on the cell tabs. Busbars, 
PCB and/or other parts that are connected with the cell tabs must have 
a separate mounting from the cell tabs.
To be able to fulfill EV5.5.11, the number of cells mechanically attached in series
is limited.
The number of cells in series can be determined based on the following explanation:
If cells are supported on both sides, i.e. between
supports, the number of cells mechanically in 
series is the number of cells between the supports
divided by 2.
(Left image)
If cells are supported from one side only, the
overall number of cells attached to that support
shall be considered the cells mechanically in series.
(Right image)
BACK
guidance.EV5.5.12 Guidance Notes:
FRICTION-BASED CELL FIXATION GUIDANCE NOTES
For friction based cell fixation, i.e. using a preload force to clamp the cells, testing is
required to determine the coefficient of friction between the cells and the material
they are attached to.
A suggestion for a test setup is shown below.
Cell or mockup
For the test, you can use a an actual cell (respecting all necessary safety measures) 
or a representative cell mockup.
If a mockup is used, it must have respresentative size (area of friction), surface condition,
and stiffness as the actual cell. Pouch cell foil may be available at the manufacturer.
Testing Pressure
The coefficient of friction may be non-linear towards the application pressure. This
must be respected in the testing and calculation.
However, the actual pressure in the stack may be inappropriate/too high for the test.
Conduct tests with different testing pressure values and then extrapolate in the 
calculation to your real application pressure.
Testing procedure and documentation
For each testing pressure, also conduct multiple tests to exclude random influences.
Document every test result in the EV5.5.10-12 Cell Fixation tab in a table.
Show pictures of and describe your test setup. Briefly summarize your test and
argue, which coefficient of friction was chosen.
BACK

ACCUMULATOR CONTAINER ATTACHMENT GUIDANCE NOTES
Please note:
Analytical calculations always preferred

Showing some flashy and colourful FEM images without legends, full model description or lettertypes are unreadable, nothing given about the meshing etc. result in a "FAIL" directly.
